correctness.rationale: Projecting the ambient basis squares by a linear retraction onto the embedded algebra preserves multiplication of embedded elements and makes the image an ideal. With this reduction, comparing coordinates gives the symmetric bilinear decomposition, and conversely the forms define an embedding since a vector killed by all forms has a*1=0. This uses the full multiplication tensor in characteristic two. Its four symmetric slices have independent anti-diagonals. Proportional forms combine, and any subset of at most seven projective forms can be padded to seven. Hence a seven-term solution requires a quotient span of rank at most three. An independent finite reproduction enumerated all rank-three spans of triples of quotient residues, extending smaller possibilities inside their full span, then tested all seven-subsets in the flats containing at least seven forms. There were 1 and 154 such flats for the two fields, respectively, and 1 and 2355 distinct seven-subsets; none contains the four target matrices. The reproduction also directly evaluated all 40 matrix-slice entries from each printed witness, verifying the exact upper bound in both fields.
residual_risks: This establishes the symmetric-factor rank over the two specified fields, not ordinary bilinear rank, other lengths or other fields.

originality.rationale: The two-field finding as submitted does not establish a distinct exact result. Its binary half, including both the full bilinear reduction and the exact lower and upper certificates, is covered by an indexed stronger initial-profile theorem not acknowledged in the frozen record. Another distinct indexed finding establishes the exact ternary minimum via characteristic-three polarization with a different witness and an exact quotient-flat census. Its indexed date is later, so that overlap is not evidence of earlier ternary priority. The primary paper alone does leave the ternary value open. The joint presentation, quotient pruning, and additional witness tables do not give a genuinely distinct classification or threshold relative to the verified exact coverage.
residual_risks: The indexed ternary match does not determine historical priority.
Broader multiplication lower-bound literature was not exhaustively checked; the cited Bläser full text and original Alder–Strassen material were not retrieved.

value.rationale: The exact small-field thresholds in the natural initial truncated-polynomial family are useful as benchmarks for any small-field classification. In particular, the ternary certificate closes the gap left by the strict >7 observation in the cited evolution-algebra paper; the binary setting tests the genuinely different characteristic-two bilinear reduction. This assesses the mathematical question and data, not the record's distinctness against the matching indexed results.
